name: fs-tooldirs-read
note: THE `./writable` GRANT IS CWD VISIBILITY, NOT PART OF THE TOOLDIRS SURFACE UNDER TEST. `backend/linux.rs::validate_cwd_visibility` refuses a RootView::Minimal launch whose cwd no rule covers, and `$tooldirs` grants only home cache dirs -- so without this the sandbox was refused before the child ever ran (rc=1, no marker written) and every assertion below was unreachable. The guard is deliberate and unit-pinned in that same file. `./writable` is granted rather than the project root because validate_cwd_visibility accepts a grant BELOW the cwd (this is why the fs-write-confine fixture launches), which restores visibility WITHOUT covering `proj/secret.txt` -- the deny this fixture exists to assert. Tree::new always materializes proj/writable, so the grant resolves in every run. `$tooldirs` grants read on the package-manager / toolchain cache dirs so a build can resolve deps from the store, while an ungranted project path stays denied. The nub store/cache anchors track the NUB embedder profile (data_namespace=nub, cache_namespace=nub/pm); XDG_CACHE_HOME is pointed at the fixture home by the harness, so $cache resolves under it. macOS/Linux only — the Windows AppContainer allowlist cannot carve the compiler's .env* read-deny out of the grant (covered by the other fs fixtures' fail-closed path).
